topic.source_contract: Natural England protected-site designation and consultation-screening layers

facts.scope_guard: Ramsar designation is protected-site evidence and not an automatic planning refusal, title or candidate-specific HRA conclusion.
SPA classification requires proposal-specific assessment and is not a generic parcel score or automatic refusal.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government - Planning Data

facts.origin: contains some MHCLG-created data pending authoritative replacement
facts.scope_guard: Single-provider aggregated SAC coverage and older source freshness require direct Natural England/JNCC cross-check for candidate use.
An SSSI unit is a management and condition subdivision and is not a separate designation, title parcel or development unit.

facts.purpose: help LPAs identify proposals likely to affect terrestrial SSSIs and when to consult Natural England
facts.basis: site feature sensitivities and development types
facts.scope_guard: An IRZ intersection is a consultation screen and not an adverse-effect finding, refusal or designation boundary.

scope_guards: Listed Ramsar and classified SPA records exclude proposed sites; status fields are not silently merged.
Ramsar, SPA, SAC and SSSI are distinct designation regimes and their geometries are not summed into a generic score.
The Planning Data SAC layer has one provider and older new-data freshness and therefore is not treated as complete current authority evidence.
SSSI units are condition and management subdivisions and are not separate statutory designations or title parcels.
SSSI Impact Risk Zones identify consultation triggers and do not prove adverse effects or planning refusal.
Designation geometry mapped against OS data is not an HMLR title or exact project red-line.
Download/API availability and update dates do not prove a candidate-specific overlay or Habitats assessment.
No score or promotion is written without exact site geometry, executed overlays and proposal-specific ecological assessment.
